# Bowra

> Verified Intelligence for business analysis: inspectable sources, numeric provenance, controlled calculations, reusable Agents, and reports your team can review.

Bowra is the self-hosted Community edition of Bowhead. This repository is a source preview. It has no commercial activation key or built-in user-count cap; operators supply infrastructure, models, credentials, and configured usage budgets. Package names and BOWHEAD_* configuration remain stable for compatibility.

## Start here

- [Project overview](README.md): capabilities, Community scope, and availability.
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): first run, knowledge, reports, Agents, MCP, automation, and contribution.
- [External-agent adoption guide](docs/agent-guide.md): capability/input/output/prerequisite/status map and actual Agent Developer API discovery.
- [Build and setup](deploy/README.md): authoritative source commands, compatible executor requirements, and export dependencies.
- [First-owner setup](deploy/community-setup.md): initialize a fresh Community installation.
- [Examples](examples/community/README.md): start with a bounded task and inspect its evidence.

## Integration facts

- MCP provides connected tools to Bowra's Agents. A supported externally callable Bowra MCP server or general task-delegation API is not published in this source preview.
- The scoped Agent Developer API base path is /api/openapi/v1 under the operator-provided service address, including any configured path prefix.
- Discover actual availability at /api/openapi/v1/reference.md. With an authorized bearer token, GET /api/openapi/v1/scopes returns granted installed scopes. Check the reference for enabled endpoints as well.
- Agent version automation requires deployment opt-in, an authorized API key, and an Agent-specific owner grant. Local Developer API transport is available; SaaS transport requires separate operator opt-in.
- Automation may submit proposals, prepare owner-accepted candidates, run permitted evaluations, and read readiness. It cannot accept proposals, confirm risks, or release on the owner's behalf.
- Citations and successful execution support verification; they do not guarantee correct conclusions. Preserve evidence gaps, assumptions, units, time ranges, and access boundaries.
- Source checkout availability does not imply a published runtime image, hosted endpoint, or validated external integration.
